findings.title: Active relocation commits and re-lists the Library before the new folder's sync state is detected
findings.body:
For the active workspace, `relocateWorkspace` goes through `relocateActive`. That calls `afterCommit` (`switch-transaction.ts:136`), which reopens the gate and sends `library:changed` (`index.ts:524-530`). The new `syncStates.refresh(current)` runs only after that, at line 755. Until it finishes, `syncStates.of(active)` has no cached result for the new path, so it falls back to the path rule (`sync-state.ts:26-30`). The path rule does not recognise a Drive folder that only the xattr identifies (`synced-folder.ts:83-91`). For up to about 4 s (the 2 s realpath bound plus the 2 s xattr bound), `activeEvictionProbe()` and `syncedStagingFor()` treat that folder as unsynced.

The Library list built from that commit's broadcast has no eviction info. Nothing lists it again afterwards: after the refresh, line 759 sends only `broadcastState()`, not `broadcastLibraryChanged()`. So evicted items keep a thumbnail URL and stay draggable and movable until something else re-lists the Library. That is the case decision 15 is meant to stop.

Two fixes:
- Detect the chosen folder before the transaction commits (refresh with the resolved `chosen` path before `relocateWorkspace`).
- Or call `host?.broadcastLibraryChanged()` after the refresh when the provider differs from what the path rule said.

For a non-active workspace the order is harmless, because nothing lists it in between.

contracts.action: relocateFolder now re-detects the sync provider of the relocated folder, probes availability bounded, and returns the workspace view
contracts.equivalent_path: addWorkspace (index.ts:577-612) and createWorkspace (index.ts:628-647) call syncStates.refresh(outcome.entry) right after the registry change, then availabilityOf, then broadcastState, and return toWorkspaceView(..., syncStates.of(entry))
contracts.before_after: The siblings run refresh before any switch: addWorkspace refreshes at line 578 before runSwitch at 601, and createWorkspace at 630 before runSwitch at 635. So the switch's afterCommit re-lists the Library with the correct sync state. relocateFolder runs refresh after relocateWorkspace, and for the active workspace that has already committed and sent library:changed (switch-transaction.ts:136, index.ts:524-530). The new code reads reg.get(id) to get the updated path (line 754), and it does use the entry the switch committed.
contracts.visible_effect: The returned `workspace` view carries the detected provider and availability, and broadcastState (line 759) updates the switcher and Settings row through listState, which uses syncStates.of(current) (index.ts:467-468). The Library itself is not re-listed after the refresh.
contracts.failure_mode: syncStates.refresh never rejects: detectSync wraps realpath and the xattr probe in withTimeout, which catches rejections and falls back (synced-folder.ts:46-56, 75-92). availabilityOf is bounded at 5 s for synced folders (index.ts:176-193, sync-state.ts:55-57). Worst case, the IPC answer is delayed by about 4 s of detection plus 5 s of probing. In the gap between commit and refresh, an xattr-only Drive folder reads as unsynced (see finding).

structuredOutput.summary:
The only change in this round is in `relocateFolder` (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts`). After a relocation, it now detects the sync provider of the new folder, runs a bounded availability probe, and returns the workspace view. That matches what add and create do, and none of the new calls can reject.

I'm raising one point, as "consider" at medium confidence, at line 755. For the active workspace, the relocation commits and sends `library:changed` before the sync detection runs. Add and create do it the other way round. In between, a Google Drive folder that is recognised only by its xattr reads as not synced. The Library list built at that moment has no eviction info, and nothing re-lists it after detection finishes.

None of the open threads are on this file, so there are no thread replies.
